title: Machine learning screens traditional Chinese medicine compounds against SARS-CoV-2
summary: Random forest and SVM models trained on ChEMBL anti-SARS-CoV-2 bioactivity data reached AUC values of 0.90 and predicted 1011 active compounds from the TCMSP database. Six compounds with highly potent predicted activity were confirmed in anti-SARS-CoV-2 experiments. Assay details were not reviewed.
ai_technology: Random forest and support vector machine activity prediction models
organization: State Key Laboratory of Primate Biomedical Research, Institute of Primate Translational Medicine, Kunming University of Science and Technology, Kunming, China

evidence.tested: Benchmark prediction with AUC 0.90, followed by experimental confirmation of six compounds.
evidence.unknown: Mechanism, potency relative to approved antivirals and clinical relevance; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning models predicted antiviral activity and prioritized compounds for testing.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from the review input and author affiliations from Crossref metadata for this DOI. Publisher full text not accessed.
